audit_status.source_base: Greek 2 Corinthians text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for mercy/service, veiled gospel, light in hearts, treasure in clay vessels, death/life of Jesus, outer wasting/inner renewal, seen/unseen.

verses.restored: Because of this, having this service/ministry, just as we were shown mercy, we do not lose heart.

familiar.text: Therefore seeing we have this ministry, as we have received mercy, we faint not;

modern.text: Therefore, since God in His mercy has given us this ministry, we do not lose heart.

original.text: Διὰ τοῦτο, ἔχοντες τὴν διακονίαν ταύτην καθὼς ἠλεήθημεν, οὐκ ⸀ἐγκακοῦμεν,

verses.restored: But we renounced the hidden things of shame, not walking in craftiness nor falsifying the word of the Divine, but by manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every human conscience before the Divine.

familiar.text: But have renounced the hidden things of dishonesty, not walking in craftiness, nor handling the word of God deceitfully; but by manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every man’s conscience in the sight of God.

modern.text: Instead, we have renounced secret and shameful ways. We do not practice deceit, nor do we distort the word of God. On the contrary, by open proclamation of the truth, we commend ourselves to every man’s conscience in the sight of God.

original.text: ἀλλὰ ἀπειπάμεθα τὰ κρυπτὰ τῆς αἰσχύνης, μὴ περιπατοῦντες ἐν πανουργίᾳ μηδὲ δολοῦντες τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ, ἀλλὰ τῇ φανερώσει τῆς ἀληθείας ⸀συνιστάνοντες ἑαυτοὺς πρὸς πᾶσαν συνείδησιν ἀνθρώπων ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.restored: And if our good news is veiled, it is veiled among those perishing,

familiar.text: But if our gospel be hid, it is hid to them that are lost:

modern.text: And even if our gospel is veiled, it is veiled to those who are perishing.

original.text: εἰ δὲ καὶ ἔστιν κεκαλυμμένον τὸ εὐαγγέλιον ἡμῶν, ἐν τοῖς ἀπολλυμένοις ἐστὶν κεκαλυμμένον,

verses.restored: in whom the god of this age blinded the thoughts of the untrusting, so that the illumination of the good news of the glory of Messiah, who is image of the Divine, might not shine.

familiar.text: In whom the god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not, lest the light of the glorious gospel of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine unto them.

modern.text: The god of this age has blinded the minds of unbelievers so they cannot see the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God.

original.text: ἐν οἷς ὁ θεὸς τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου ἐτύφλωσεν τὰ νοήματα τῶν ἀπίστων εἰς τὸ μὴ ⸀αὐγάσαι τὸν φωτισμὸν τοῦ εὐαγγελίου τῆς δόξης τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὅς ἐστιν εἰκὼν τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.restored: For we do not proclaim ourselves, but Jesus Messiah as Lord, and ourselves as your servants because of Jesus.

familiar.text: For we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants for Jesus’ sake.

modern.text: For we do not proclaim ourselves, but Jesus Christ as Lord, and ourselves as your servants for Jesus’ sake.

original.text: οὐ γὰρ ἑαυτοὺς κηρύσσομεν ἀλλὰ ⸂Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν⸃ κύριον, ἑαυτοὺς δὲ δούλους ὑμῶν διὰ Ἰησοῦν.

verses.restored: Because the Divine who said, Out of darkness light will shine, is the One who shone in our hearts for illumination of the knowledge of the glory of the Divine in the face of Jesus Messiah.

familiar.text: For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.

modern.text: For God, who said, “Let light shine out of darkness,” made His light shine in our hearts to give us the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ. Treasure in Jars of Clay (Romans 6:1–14)

original.text: ὅτι ὁ θεὸς ὁ εἰπών· Ἐκ σκότους φῶς ⸀λάμψει, ὃς ἔλαμψεν ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ἡμῶν πρὸς φωτισμὸν τῆς γνώσεως τῆς δόξης τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν προσώπῳ ⸀Χριστοῦ.

verses.restored: But we have this treasure in clay vessels, so that the surpassing power may be of the Divine and not from us.

familiar.text: But we have this treasure in earthen vessels, that the excellency of the power may be of God, and not of us.

modern.text: Now we have this treasure in jars of clay to show that this surpassingly great power is from God and not from us.

original.text: Ἔχομεν δὲ τὸν θησαυρὸν τοῦτον ἐν ὀστρακίνοις σκεύεσιν, ἵνα ἡ ὑπερβολὴ τῆς δυνάμεως ᾖ τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ μὴ ἐξ ἡμῶν·

verses.restored: In every way pressured, but not crushed; perplexed, but not despairing;

familiar.text: We are troubled on every side, yet not distressed; we are perplexed, but not in despair;

modern.text: We are hard pressed on all sides, but not crushed; perplexed, but not in despair;

original.text: ἐν παντὶ θλιβόμενοι ἀλλʼ οὐ στενοχωρούμενοι, ἀπορούμενοι ἀλλʼ οὐκ ἐξαπορούμενοι,

verses.restored: pursued/persecuted, but not abandoned; struck down, but not destroyed;

familiar.text: Persecuted, but not forsaken; cast down, but not destroyed;

modern.text: persecuted, but not forsaken; struck down, but not destroyed.

original.text: διωκόμενοι ἀλλʼ οὐκ ἐγκαταλειπόμενοι, καταβαλλόμενοι ἀλλʼ οὐκ ἀπολλύμενοι,

verses.restored: always carrying around in the body the dying of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be made manifest in our body.

familiar.text: Always bearing about in the body the dying of the Lord Jesus, that the life also of Jesus might be made manifest in our body.

modern.text: We always carry around in our body the death of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our body.

original.text: πάντοτε τὴν νέκρωσιν ⸀τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἐν τῷ σώματι περιφέροντες, ἵνα καὶ ἡ ζωὴ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἐν τῷ σώματι ἡμῶν φανερωθῇ·

verses.restored: For we who live are always being handed over to death because of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus also may be made manifest in our mortal flesh.

familiar.text: For we which live are alway delivered unto death for Jesus’ sake, that the life also of Jesus might be made manifest in our mortal flesh.

modern.text: For we who are alive are always consigned to death for Jesus’ sake, so that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our mortal body.

original.text: ἀεὶ γὰρ ἡμεῖς οἱ ζῶντες εἰς θάνατον παραδιδόμεθα διὰ Ἰησοῦν, ἵνα καὶ ἡ ζωὴ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ φανερωθῇ ἐν τῇ θνητῇ σαρκὶ ἡμῶν.

verses.restored: So then death works in us, but life in you.

familiar.text: So then death worketh in us, but life in you.

modern.text: So then, death is at work in us, but life is at work in you.

original.text: ὥστε ⸀ὁ θάνατος ἐν ἡμῖν ἐνεργεῖται, ἡ δὲ ζωὴ ἐν ὑμῖν.

verses.restored: Having the same spirit of trust according to what has been written, I trusted, therefore I spoke, we also trust, therefore we also speak,

familiar.text: We having the same spirit of faith, according as it is written, I believed, and therefore have I spoken; we also believe, and therefore speak;

modern.text: And in keeping with what is written: “I believed, therefore I have spoken,” we who have the same spirit of faith also believe and therefore speak,

original.text: Ἔχοντες δὲ τὸ αὐτὸ πνεῦμα τῆς πίστεως, κατὰ τὸ γεγραμμένον· Ἐπίστευσα, διὸ ἐλάλησα, καὶ ἡμεῖς πιστεύομεν, διὸ καὶ λαλοῦμεν,

verses.restored: knowing that the One who raised the Lord Jesus will also raise us with Jesus and present us with you.

familiar.text: Knowing that he which raised up the Lord Jesus shall raise up us also by Jesus, and shall present us with you.

modern.text: knowing that the One who raised the Lord Jesus will also raise us with Jesus and present us with you in His presence.

original.text: εἰδότες ὅτι ὁ ἐγείρας ⸀τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ ἡμᾶς ⸀σὺν Ἰησοῦ ἐγερεῖ καὶ παραστήσει σὺν ὑμῖν.

verses.restored: For all things are because of you, so that grace, having increased through the many, may cause thanksgiving to abound into the glory of the Divine.

familiar.text: For all things are for your sakes, that the abundant grace might through the thanksgiving of many redound to the glory of God.

modern.text: All this is for your benefit, so that the grace that is extending to more and more people may overflow in thanksgiving, to the glory of God.

original.text: τὰ γὰρ πάντα διʼ ὑμᾶς, ἵνα ἡ χάρις πλεονάσασα διὰ τῶν πλειόνων τὴν εὐχαριστίαν περισσεύσῃ εἰς τὴν δόξαν τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.restored: Therefore we do not lose heart; but even if our outer human is being decayed, yet our inner human is being renewed day by day.

familiar.text: For which cause we faint not; but though our outward man perish, yet the inward man is renewed day by day.

modern.text: Therefore we do not lose heart. Though our outer self is wasting away, yet our inner self is being renewed day by day.

original.text: Διὸ οὐκ ⸀ἐγκακοῦμεν, ἀλλʼ εἰ καὶ ὁ ἔξω ἡμῶν ἄνθρωπος διαφθείρεται, ἀλλʼ ὁ ⸂ἔσω ἡμῶν⸃ ἀνακαινοῦται ἡμέρᾳ καὶ ἡμέρᾳ.

verses.restored: For the momentary lightness of our pressure is working for us an age-long weight of glory beyond measure upon measure,

familiar.text: For our light affliction, which is but for a moment, worketh for us a far more exceeding and eternal weight of glory;

modern.text: For our light and momentary affliction is producing for us an eternal glory that is far beyond comparison.

original.text: τὸ γὰρ παραυτίκα ἐλαφρὸν τῆς θλίψεως ⸀ἡμῶν καθʼ ὑπερβολὴν εἰς ὑπερβολὴν αἰώνιον βάρος δόξης κατεργάζεται ἡμῖν,

verses.restored: while we do not look at the things seen, but the things not seen; for the things seen are temporary, but the things not seen are age-long.

familiar.text: While we look not at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen: for the things which are seen are temporal; but the things which are not seen are eternal.

modern.text: So we fix our eyes not on what is seen, but on what is unseen. For what is seen is temporary, but what is unseen is eternal.

original.text: μὴ σκοπούντων ἡμῶν τὰ βλεπόμενα ἀλλὰ τὰ μὴ βλεπόμενα, τὰ γὰρ βλεπόμενα πρόσκαιρα, τὰ δὲ μὴ βλεπόμενα αἰώνια.

translation_notes: Treasure in clay vessels is not body-hatred; the vulnerable body becomes the site where Divine power is made visible.
Outer decay and inner renewal should be held together with resurrection hope, not used to despise embodiment.
